input.strategy_title: Idle resource reporting in the web console
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Cluster administrators cannot see which resources are sitting idle: workbenches
nobody has touched in weeks keep their volumes and reservations, and old
pipeline runs accumulate storage. Admins ask for a single report in the RHOAI
web console showing idle and stale resources per project so they can reclaim
capacity with confidence. The notebook controller already tracks last-activity
timestamps, and Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata — the data
exists; it is just not surfaced anywhere.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P1 | The web console shows a per-project idle-workbench report (last activity, owner, reserved resources), sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | The web console shows a stale pipeline-run report (completed runs older than a configurable age with retained artifacts), sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata. |
| HLR-3 | P2 | Administrators can export either report as CSV. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps. |

## Affected Components

- RHOAI web console
- Notebook controller
- Kubeflow Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automated reclamation or deletion of idle resources
- Cost/chargeback calculations

## Open Questions

None.

# Console idle and stale resource reports with CSV export

## Description

This epic delivers the idle resource reporting capability in the RHOAI web
console: a per-project idle-workbench report and a stale pipeline-run report,
plus CSV export of either report. Cluster administrators get a single place in
the console to see which resources are sitting idle — workbenches nobody has
touched in weeks that keep their volumes and reservations, and old pipeline
runs accumulating storage — so they can reclaim capacity with confidence. The
data already exists on the platform (the notebook controller tracks
last-activity timestamps; Kubeflow Pipelines retains run completion metadata);
this epic surfaces it, it does not build new data collection.

## Scope

- Per-project idle-workbench report in the web console, showing per workbench:
  - last activity, sourced from the notebook controller's activity tracking
  - owner
  - reserved resources
- Stale pipeline-run report in the web console, showing per project:
  - completed runs older than a configurable age
  - retained artifacts associated with those runs
  - sourced from Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata
- The stale-run age threshold is configurable by administrators
- CSV export of either report (workbench report or pipeline-run report)
- Reports are read-only views; no reclamation or deletion actions (explicitly
  out of scope in the strategy)

The notebook controller and Kubeflow Pipelines components undergo no code
changes in this epic; they are consumed as-is. Demonstrating that the console
can read the notebook controller's last-activity data and the Kubeflow
Pipelines run completion metadata is part of this epic's verification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a project containing workbenches, when an administrator opens the
  idle-workbench report, then it lists each workbench with its last activity
  (from the notebook controller's activity tracking), owner, and reserved
  resources.
- Given a project containing pipeline runs, when an administrator opens the
  stale pipeline-run report with a configured age threshold, then it lists the
  completed runs older than that age together with their retained artifacts,
  and the listed runs match the Kubeflow Pipelines run metadata.
- Given a configured stale-run age threshold, when an administrator changes
  it, then the stale pipeline-run report reflects the new threshold without
  requiring a console redeployment.
- Given either report, when an administrator exports it, then a CSV file is
  produced containing the same rows and columns as the on-screen report.
- The reports introduce no reclamation or deletion actions (read-only).
- The console build and existing test suite pass with the new reports included.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P1): per-project idle-workbench report — covered by this epic.
- HLR-2 (P1): stale pipeline-run report — covered by this epic.
- HLR-3 (P2): CSV export of either report — covered by this epic. Bundled with
  the P1 report work rather than split: the export acts on the same report UI
  surfaces and data structures, so it is not independently deferrable and
  splitting it would force a second pass over the same report views.

# Document the idle/stale resource reports and safe reclamation steps

## Description

This epic delivers the documentation for the console's idle resource reporting
capability: product documentation that explains the idle-workbench report and
the stale pipeline-run report (what each column means, where the data comes
from, and how to configure the stale-run age threshold) and walks
administrators through safe reclamation steps — how to act on the reports to
reclaim capacity without disrupting active work. The documentation is authored
after the console reports exist, against what was actually implemented.

## Scope

Content outline (topics to author within this epic):

- A doc topic introducing idle resource reporting in the RHOAI web console:
  what the reports are for and who they are for (cluster administrators)
- Reference documentation for the per-project idle-workbench report: columns
  (last activity, owner, reserved resources) and the notebook controller
  activity data it is sourced from
- Reference documentation for the stale pipeline-run report: columns, the
  configurable age threshold (how to view and change it), and the Kubeflow
  Pipelines run metadata it is sourced from
- Reference documentation for CSV export of either report
- A procedural topic on safe reclamation: how an administrator uses the
  reports to identify idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs and the safe
  manual steps to reclaim the underlying volumes, reservations, and artifact
  storage — including what to check before deleting (recent activity, run
  ownership) and what is intentionally not automated
- Explicit statement of the boundaries: automated reclamation/deletion and
  cost/chargeback calculations are not part of the feature

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation explains both reports (idle-workbench and stale
  pipeline-run), including every column each report displays and where its
  data comes from.
- Published documentation explains how to configure the stale-run age
  threshold and how to export either report as CSV.
- Published documentation provides step-by-step safe reclamation guidance for
  idle workbenches and stale pipeline runs, including pre-deletion checks.
- Published documentation has been technically reviewed against the
  implemented console reports (reviewed by or with the implementing team) so
  that every documented behavior matches the shipped feature.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation explains the reports and safe reclamation steps —
  covered by this epic.
